name: FNPS Conservation Grant
summary: Grants of up to $5,000 for one year for applied conservation of rare or imperiled native plants and plant communities in Florida. A project must be sponsored by a chapter of the Florida Native Plant Society.

amount.note: For a 1-year period; may reapply in following years

eligibility.rule: Project preserves, conserves, or restores rare or imperiled native plant taxa or plant communities
Project is sponsored by an FNPS Chapter
Does not plant outside the historical range or native habitat of the species

status.quote: To qualify for a Conservation Grant, the proposed project must be sponsored by an FNPS Chapter. Contact: conservation@fnps.org Application Deadline: March 5, 2027

amount.quote: FNPS Conservation Grants support applied conservation projects for Florida’s native plants. Grants of up to $5,000 fund one-year projects, and applicants who need support beyond one year may reapply in later years.

eligibility.quote: Projects must help preserve, conserve, or restore rare or imperiled native plant taxa or plant communities.
To qualify for a Conservation Grant, the proposed project must be sponsored by an FNPS Chapter.

The Conservation Committee will not fund projects that install plants or germplasm (any plant material from which a plant can be propagated): • Outside the species’ historical range, or • Outside the species’ native habitat or plant community.

effort.quote: Submit completed applications by March 5, 2027, at 5 p.m. EST to be considered for the 2027 grant cycle.

after_award.quote: After completing the project, the recipient must share the results, with photographs, in two ways: (1) a written summary in the FNPS publication, the Palmetto, and (2) a presentation at the biennial FNPS Conference, typically held in May, or at a monthly FNPS chapter meeting.
